limits: Walmart reports as a retailer with a seasonal business; figures are for the fiscal year ended January 31, 2026 only, as requested.

Total financial debt includes a 750 variable-rate note and foreign-held debt as reported; the report notes long-term debt carrying value of 38,166 (Note 7) which agrees with the balance sheet components.
Operating margin uses total revenues (713,163) per the rule. The company's published 4.2% margin uses net sales. Confirm which basis the analyst wants.

Net debt excludes operating lease obligations (1,631 current + 13,941 long-term) and finance lease obligations (856 current + 5,905 long-term), per the rule. Including them would materially raise leverage; the analyst should decide whether to add them.
Cash excludes 'restricted cash' (the cash-flow statement total is 11,321 versus balance sheet cash of 10,727). The rule specifies cash and cash equivalents only.
Diluted EPS is 2.73 per the statement of income; the MD&A uses the same figure. Net income of 21,893 is attributable to Walmart; the report's ROA calculation uses consolidated net income of 22,270.
Capex is taken as purchases of property and equipment (26,642). The report's total capex by segment table also shows 26,642, so there is no reconciling difference.

The report includes a PhonePe share-based compensation charge of about 0.7 billion and a net gain on investments of 2.1 billion in other gains and losses, which affect comparability of net income. These are not adjusted here, since the rule asks for figures as published.
Page numbers are the printed page numbers in the filing text. Some figures are from the MD&A (Item 7) and from the notes (Item 8) and are cross-checked where possible.
